task_description: The script identifies surface water frequency (swf) by applying a cloud-masked MOD09GA dataset, calculating AWEI (Automated Water Extraction Index) for each image, thresholding AWEI with -0.1 to classify water, and computing the mean water occurrence over time. It then analyzes vegetation indices (NDVI/EVI) within areas of moderate water presence (0.3 < swf < 0.9) using MOD13Q1 data.

The script identifies maize cultivation areas in 2018 for three regions (Liaoning, Jilin, and Heilongjiang provinces) using threshold-based classification of MTCI-derived vegetation indices, masked by cropland and rice exclusion layers. The output is a binary raster indicating maize presence.

The script detects wildfire-affected areas by computing the differenced Normalized Burn Ratio (dNBR) from pre- and post-fire Landsat 8 surface reflectance imagery, using cloud-masked composites and a fire perimeter buffer to isolate burned regions, outputting a binary mask of burn scars thresholded at dNBR > 0.44.

The script detects surface water by computing NDWI from Sentinel-2 (using B3 and B8) and SDWI from Sentinel-1 (VV and VH polarizations), then combines them to compute a normalized difference between NDWI and SDWI for analysis.
task_name: Detect surface water using NDWI and SDWI

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent using MODIS Nadir Reflectance data by computing multiple water indices (AWEI, mNDWI, LSWI) and vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI), then applying a water frequency thresholding method based on the AjianB and AjianC metrics. The output is a mean water frequency map (WV_swf and MODIS_swf) representing the temporal occurrence of surface water over the study period.

The script calculates and compares Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) from pre- and post-fire Landsat imagery to assess vegetation loss and burn severity, outputting a difference layer and histogram for analysis.

The script calculates the monthly surface water frequency (SWF) from MODIS MOD13Q1 data over a one-year period (2000–2001) using the Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI), classifies SWF into four thresholds (≥0.75, ≥0.5–<0.75, ≥0.25–<0.5, <0.25), computes the area of each class within a region, and identifies wetlands by combining EVI and NDVI thresholds with SWF. It outputs the mean SWF map, classified SWF layers, their respective areas in km², and the wetland extent with area.

The script calculates the area (in km²) of different land cover and crop types within a user-defined region of interest by extracting grouped pixel counts from the USDA Cropland Data Layer (CDL) 2014 and NLCD 2011 datasets. It sorts the resulting class areas in descending order by class label and prints the top five largest classes.
task_name: Analyze crop and land cover distribution

task_description: The script converts a feature collection of the Utcubamba region with COUNT attributes into a raster image, where each pixel represents the first value of the COUNT property, and reprojects the resulting raster to a 30-meter scale using its original CRS.

The script calculates the frequency of surface water occurrence by analyzing NDVI values from MODIS MOD09Q1 data over 2019, identifying pixels with NDVI < 0 as water, and computing their mean across the time series to generate a surface water frequency (swf) map.

The script calculates Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC) using median Sentinel-2 surface reflectance imagery from 2019, masking water via NDVI thresholding and applying a percentile-based normalization method over the XJZZQ region.

The script computes Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on a cloud-filtered, atmospherically corrected mosaic of Sentinel satellite imagery over a specified region, using 11 spectral bands. It centers the data by subtracting mean values, calculates eigenvalues and eigenvectors from the covariance matrix, and outputs standardized principal component bands. The percentage of variance explained by each principal component is printed for interpretability.
task_name: Compute principal components of Sentinel bands

task_description: The script classifies land cover into six distinct classes (Agriculture, Urban, Bare Soil, Water, Forest, and Other Vegetation) using a Random Forest classifier applied to a cloud-free Sentinel-2 mosaic. The output is a classified raster map with accuracy assessment from training and validation datasets.

The script calculates the Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI) from MODIS MOD09GA data to detect surface water, masks clouds using the state_1km band, and computes the mean water occurrence over a specified date range and region, resulting in a surface water frequency map.

The script calculates the mean NDSI snow cover from MODIS MOD10A1 data for December 2022, masks values above 5 to identify significant snow cover, clips the result to the Cordillera Blanca region in Peru, and computes the total area (in square meters) of detected snow cover within that polygon.

The script calculates the Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI) from MODIS Nadir Reflectance data to identify surface water extent over a one-year period, then computes the mean water occurrence frequency (swf) as a continuous surface representing how frequently water was detected. It also extracts AWEI time series values at specific point locations for further analysis.

The script calculates the Soil-Adjusted Vegetation Index (SAVI) from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to assess vegetation health and density over a specified region in 2020, applying cloud and cloud shadow masking for improved accuracy. The output is a mean annual SAVI composite image.

The script identifies surface water extent by applying a multi-condition threshold and band ratio method on Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, specifically leveraging SWIR1 and SWIR2 bands and their relationships with visible and NIR bands during autumn 2019. The output is a binary mask layer indicating water presence based on spectral inequalities and magnitude thresholds.
task_name: Identify surface water using SWIR bands

task_description: The script extracts surface water extent from the JRC Global Surface Water dataset for January 2019 by filtering the MonthlyHistory collection, identifying pixels classified as 'water' (value 2), masking and clipping to a user-defined geometry ('table'), and computing the total water area in square kilometers using pixel area summation.

The script classifies land cover into five classes (urban, agricultural, water, forest, and other natural vegetation) using a Random Forest classifier trained on manually labeled polygons. The output is a classified raster map derived from a Sentinel-2 cloud-free mosaic.

The script calculates the frequency of surface water occurrence by combining Landsat 5 and 7 collections over a specified time period. It applies a cloud mask, computes two water indices (AWEInsh and AWEIsh), identifies water pixels using a threshold, and then computes the ratio of water observations to total observations across both sensors to produce a surface water frequency (SWF) map.
The script calculates NDVI from cloud-removed Landsat 8 TOA reflectance data over Pune between July 25 and September 25, 2019, producing a cloud-corrected vegetation index map of the area.

The script identifies surface water frequency and vegetation cover by analyzing Sentinel-2 imagery from March 2019 to February 2020. It computes NDVI, mNDWI, and EVI indices, derives water features using thresholded combinations of AjianB, AjianC, and EVI, and calculates the mean water frequency (S2_swf) and vegetation fraction (S2_VF). Final outputs include a water frequency map, a vegetation fraction map, and the total vegetation area within a specified region.

The script calculates the Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (AWEI) from MODIS Nadir Reflectance bands to map surface water extent over time, then computes the mean water occurrence frequency (SWF) from March 2003 to February 2004. It identifies persistent and seasonal water bodies, masks areas with high water frequency, and extracts EVI values from permanent water regions. The output includes a water frequency map, vector polygons of non-permanent water areas, and mean EVI values within those regions.

The script classifies land cover into three categories—vegetation, water, and built-up areas—using a CART classifier trained on manually labeled regions and applied to a 2019 Landsat 8 mosaic clipped to the vij region.

The script identifies surface water frequency and vegetated fraction using MODIS MOD09GA data by calculating AWEI, NDVI, and EVI indices over March–April 2000. It outputs mean water occurrence (swf) and vegetated fraction (vef) layers, then thresholds them to estimate total water and vegetation areas within a region.
task_name: Identify surface water and vegetation fraction

task_description: The script calculates the SDG15.3.1 indicator for land degradation by combining three sub-indicators: (1) Vegetation productivity trend, state, and performance using NPP or ET data; (2) Land cover change from ESA CCI; and (3) Soil organic carbon change from SoilGrids. It produces classified maps of degradation status (improving, stable, degrading) through rule-based integration of these layers.
task_name: Assess land degradation using productivity, land cover, and soil carbon

task_description: The script identifies surface water extent and frequency by computing multiple water and vegetation indices (AWEI, mNDWI, NDVI, EVI, LSWI) from MODIS data, then applying a decision rule based on AjianB, AjianC, and EVI to derive a water mask. The final outputs are mean water frequency maps (WV_swf and MODIS_swf) over the study period.

The script calculates the Automated Water Extraction Index (AWEI) from MODIS Nadir Reflectance bands to map surface water extent over a specific region for October–November and December 2019, then computes the mean surface water frequency (SWF) as a composite of the two periods. It also calculates the total image count used in the analysis to assess data coverage.

The script computes the Synthetic Dual-Polarization Water Index (SDWI) from Sentinel-1 GRD data, specifically using VH and VV polarizations from ascending passes, then applies Canny edge detection to identify boundaries of water bodies. The output is a masked edge map highlighting sharp transitions in backscatter, likely corresponding to shorelines or water extent edges.
task_name: Detect water bodies using SDWI and edge detection

task_description: The script classifies land cover into four categories (water, irrigated grassland, natural grassland, and bare land) using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data, spectral indices (NDVI, NDWI), and a Random Forest classifier, with accuracy assessment via confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script performs a supervised land cover classification using a Random Forest classifier on Sentinel-2 or similar multispectral imagery. Training data consists of manually defined polygon regions representing five classes: agriculture (class 2), urban/built-up (class 3), bare soil (class 4), water (class 6), and vegetation (class 5). The output is a classified raster map showing spatial distribution of these land cover types, along with accuracy assessment metrics including training confusion matrix and validation error matrix.

The script calculates surface water frequency (WF) using MODIS Nadir Reflectance bands to derive NDVI, EVI, and mNDWI indices, then applies a threshold-based water detection model (AjianB and AjianC) combining mNDWI-NDVI and mNDWI-EVI differences with low EVI values to identify water presence over time. The output is a mean surface water frequency map from March 2018 to March 2019.

The script compares MODIS-derived burned areas from 2017 with NBAC (National Burned Area Composite) data over British Columbia by generating a combined classification image (NBAC + BULC), computing an error matrix through binary comparison, and extracting regional statistics for agreement/disagreement zones (00, 01, 10, 11). Outputs include classified rasters and printed area sums for each confusion matrix category.

The script models temporal land cover changes using a Bayesian updating framework (BULC) to compute posterior probabilities of class membership at each time step based on a sequence of classified satellite images. It outputs time-series probability layers, final classification maps, confidence metrics, and optional video visualizations of change.
task_name: Model land cover transitions over time

task_description: The script classifies land cover in Lagos using Sentinel-2A surface reflectance data from 2018, applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled samples. It outputs a classified map with four categories: water, forest, buildings, and wetland, computes overall accuracy via a confusion matrix using validation samples, and calculates the area (in km²) of each class within Lagos.

The script analyzes post-fire vegetation conditions using NBR derived from Landsat 5 data, applying topographic illumination correction and cloud masking to generate a cloud-free NDVI-based composite for burn severity assessment.

The script computes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from Landsat 5 and Landsat 8 surface reflectance data to analyze temporal vegetation changes using the Verdet algorithm, which detects breakpoints and trends in time series. The output includes two Verdet results: one for merged Landsat 5 and 8 collections (2008–2011 and 2013–2017), and another for Landsat 8 only (2013–2017), enabling comparison of vegetation dynamics across sensors and time periods.

The script calculates the maximum and minimum values of UN-adjusted population density over the period 2000–2021 within a specified region of interest (roi) by converting a time-series image collection into multiband imagery and applying reduction operations.

The script processes the MODIS MCD12Q1 IGBP land cover classification for January 1, 2001, reprojects it to WGS84 at 500m resolution, and applies a focal smoothing operation (focal_max → focal_min → focal_max) to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence of land cover classes.

The script identifies areas of forest disturbance between 2011 and 2014 by reclassifying a disturbance year image, then masks these areas with a change condition (change1015.eq(10)), resulting in a binary map of significant land cover change during that period within the region of interest.

The script classifies land cover into water and buildings using Sentinel-2 imagery from March to September 2020, training a CART classifier on spectral bands B2–B8 and applying it to generate a false color classification map.

The script detects cloud and cloud shadow pixels in Sentinel-2 imagery over the Qilian Mountains on November 4, 2019, using a combination of QA60 band masking, cloud scoring, and geometric shadow projection based on S5P-derived cloud top height. Outputs include a cloud mask, cloud-shadow mask, and masked Sentinel-2 images.

The script calculates the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) for the Beijing region using Landsat 8 and MODIS data from June to October 2020. It computes NDVI, NDBSI, Wet, and LST as input variables, performs PCA transformation, and generates a normalized ecological index map (RSEI) to assess regional ecological conditions.

The script identifies surface water bodies by computing the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) from a cloud-filtered median composite of optical imagery over a specified region and time period, then applying a threshold (NDWI > 0.1) to mask and highlight water pixels in blue.

The script calculates fractional vegetation cover (FVC) for grasslands using Sentinel-2 surface reflectance data from July to August 2020 and 2021, classifies FVC into five categories, extracts areas with high vegetation cover (class 5, FVC > 0.7) in 2020, and computes the change in FVC between 2020 and 2021 within those grassland areas. The output is a raster image representing the difference in high-vegetation-cover grasslands between the two years.

The script calculates dNBR to classify burn severity and computes Burn Recovery Ratio (BRR) over time across different slope classes using Landsat surface reflectance data, analyzing vegetation recovery dynamics after a fire event in Yimen.
task_name: Assess post-fire vegetation recovery by slope

task_description: The script computes a long-term average of daily precipitation from CHIRPS data for each day of the year over the period 2001–2020, then calculates anomalies by subtracting this mean from individual daily composites. It generates a 365-day climatological time series of mean daily precipitation and corresponding anomaly images, clipped to a user-defined region (table), with outputs structured as image collections representing daily precipitation patterns and deviations.

The script filters Landsat 8 surface reflectance images from 2020, removes pixels affected by clouds and cloud shadows using the pixel_qa band, and creates a mosaic of cloud-free imagery for visual comparison between raw and processed results.

The script identifies areas of land cover change within regions classified as receiving less than 200 mm/year of annual mean precipitation by combining a precipitation classification layer and a land change map. It computes the total area (in square meters) of pixels where land cover changed and precipitation is lowest, masking non-relevant areas.
task_name: Identify land cover change in low precipitation areas

task_description: The script classifies land cover types using Landsat 8 surface reflectance data by computing spectral indices (NDBI, EVI), extracting GLCM texture features, and applying a Random Forest classifier trained on labeled sample regions. It outputs a classified land cover map and evaluates accuracy using a confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and kappa coefficient.

The script calculates NDVI from surface reflectance data of Landsat 8 to analyze vegetation conditions within a specific region (kq) over the year 2020, producing a median composite image masked to the region and including NDVI as an additional band.

The script generates a composite image stack from Landsat 8 surface reflectance data for 2020, divided into three temporal periods (Jan-Apr, May-Aug, Sep-Dec), computing median composites for each period and standard deviation across the year. It calculates multiple vegetation, water, built-up, and soil indices (NDVI, EVI, GCVI, NBR, NDWI, mNDWI, NDBI, NDSI, MSAVI2, SATVI, BSI, BR) and combines them with temporal medians and inter-annual variability into a single stacked asset. The output is used for land surface monitoring and change analysis.

The script calculates the mean terrestrial water storage anomalies (lwe_thickness_csr) from GRACE satellite data over Kruger National Park (KNP) for the year 2020, providing a spatially averaged time-series reduction of groundwater equivalent water thickness.

The script selects the least cloudy Landsat 8 surface reflectance image from May to June 2016 over a specified region of interest, then extracts training samples for four land cover classes (urban, water, forest, agriculture) using six spectral bands (B2–B7). The output is a feature collection of labeled training data for supervised land cover classification.

The script masks cloud and cloud shadow pixels from Landsat 8 Surface Reflectance data over a specific region (Yellow River basin) for June 2020, then mosaics the images into a single cloud-cleared composite.

The script calculates long-term average daily precipitation from CHIRPS data (2001–2021) and computes daily precipitation anomalies for each day of the year by comparing individual year composites to the climatological mean, producing cumulative anomaly images over time within a specified region of interest.
